title: VasoDilators for Radial Artery to Optimize Graft Outcome - A Multicenter InterNational Randomized Controlled Trial
official: VasoDilators for Radial Artery to Optimize Graft Outcome - A Multicenter InterNational Randomized Controlled Trial
summary:
The DRAGON-RA study is evaluating whether taking an oral vasodilator, calcium channel blocker or nitrate, once daily for 12 months after coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) surgery using a radial artery graft affects patient outcomes compared with taking no oral vasodilator for 12 months.

The study will compare outcomes between the groups, including the condition of the bypass grafts and clinical events, using study assessments and follow-up described in the protocol.

The study's hypothesis is that treatment with an oral vasodilator after CABG may improve radial artery graft outcomes compared with no oral vasodilator. The study will also assess the safety of the treatment and collect information about participants' health during follow-up.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Age ≥18 years.
* First-time isolated coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) with use of the radial artery (RA).
* Ability to sign informed consent and comply with study procedures.

Exclusion Criteria:

* No use of the RA.
* Any concomitant cardiac or non-cardiac procedure.
* Current or expected indication for either study drug (calcium channel blockers or nitrates) where initiation or continuation of therapy is deemed clinically necessary and cannot be safely withheld.
* Known allergy or hypersensitivity to active ingredients or excipients of the intended study drug.
* Contraindications to use of the intended study drug.
* Contraindications to coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA), e.g., iodine allergy.
* Preoperative end-organ dysfunction (dialysis, moderate to severe liver failure, respiratory failure), cancer, or other non-cardiac comorbidity with life expectancy \<5 years.
* Perioperative complications precluding randomization, including but not limited to perioperative myocardial infarction, postcardiotomy cardiogenic shock, or pulmonary congestion.
* Women of childbearing potential, defined as a premenopausal female capable of becoming pregnant.
